# Spec: Three-Person Website Delivery (Six Weeks)

Status: draft
Topic: Website delivery and team management

## Purpose

Establish management requirements for a three-person team to deliver a website within a six-week timeline. This spec defines roles, ownership, decision authority, milestones, and communication practices needed for successful coordination and delivery.

## Requirements

| ID | Requirement | Acceptance criterion (Given / When / Then) | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| R1 | Team roles and responsibilities are assigned | Given the three team members, when roles are assigned, then each person has a clear primary responsibility (e.g., backend, frontend, product/QA) and knows their decision authority | open |
| R2 | A product owner or decision-maker is named | Given the project starts, when a decision must be made about scope or priority, then there is one named person who makes that decision and the team accepts it | open |
| R3 | The six-week delivery is broken into milestones | Given the six-week timeline, when a milestone is reached, then deliverables for that period have been completed and reviewed | open |
| R4 | Team members can unblock each other within one business day | Given a team member is blocked by another's work, when they request unblocking, then the other team member responds and resolves the block within one business day | open |
| R5 | Weekly progress is tracked against milestones | Given each week passes, when the weekly sync occurs, then the team reviews what was shipped, what is at risk, and what is due next | open |
| R6 | Scope decisions are made before development begins | Given ambiguity about what the website must include, when clarification is needed, then the product owner decides and the decision is recorded | open |
| R7 | Bugs found after code review are fixed before merge | Given a bug is discovered during review, when the developer is notified, then the bug is fixed within one business day before merging | open |
| R8 | Team members know the definition of done for the website | Given the six-week deadline arrives, when the website is declared complete, then all team members agree it meets the pre-agreed definition of done | open |

## Owners and Roles (RACI)

| Responsibility | Owner (UNKNOWN) | Approver | Consulted | Informed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Product scope and priority | UNKNOWN | UNKNOWN | Full team | Full team |
| Technical architecture decisions | UNKNOWN | UNKNOWN | Full team | Full team |
| QA and acceptance criteria | UNKNOWN | Product owner | Development team | Stakeholders |
| Release and deployment | UNKNOWN | Product owner | Full team | Stakeholders |
| Team velocity and risk escalation | UNKNOWN | Product owner | Full team | Stakeholders |

## Decisions and Approvers

| Decision | Who decides | Timeline | Prerequisite |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Website scope and feature list | UNKNOWN (product owner role) | Before development starts (Week 1) | UNKNOWN: stakeholder input |
| Technology stack | UNKNOWN (tech lead role) | Before development starts (Week 1) | Scope agreement |
| Definition of done and acceptance criteria | Product owner | Before development starts (Week 1) | Scope agreement |
| Major scope changes | Product owner | As requested | Weekly review meeting |

## Schedule and Milestones

| Milestone | Target week | Deliverables | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Project kickoff and planning | Week 1 | Scope document, tech stack decision, role assignments, definition of done | UNKNOWN |
| Core feature development | Weeks 2–4 | UNKNOWN: backend API, frontend pages, database schema (specifics depend on scope) | Development team |
| Integration and testing | Week 5 | All features integrated, bug fixes, QA sign-off | Development team + QA owner |
| Launch prep and deployment | Week 6 | Performance testing, deployment checklist, go/no-go decision, production release | Full team |

## Communication

- **Daily standup**: 15 minutes, same time each day. Updates: what shipped, what is blocked, what is next. Forum: UNKNOWN (in-person, Slack, video call).
- **Weekly sync**: 1 hour every Friday (or UNKNOWN: different day). Review: progress against milestones, blockers, risk, scope changes. Owner: UNKNOWN (product owner or tech lead).
- **Blocking escalation**: If a blocker is not resolved within one business day, escalate to UNKNOWN (product owner or team lead).
- **Decision log**: All decisions about scope, technology, and tradeoffs are recorded in UNKNOWN (shared document, wiki, or issue tracker).
- **Code review**: All code is reviewed by at least one other team member before merge. Turnaround: same business day where possible.

## Non-goals

- Training on new technologies; assume team members arrive with required skills.
- Handling requests for features outside the initial scope (these are recorded but deferred post-launch).
- Formal project management overhead; sprints, Jira, or other PMO tools are not assumed.
- Building internal tools, design systems, or CI/CD pipelines beyond what is needed for this project.

## Open questions

- **UNKNOWN**: Who is the product owner / decision-maker? What is their availability?
- **UNKNOWN**: What is the website? (e.g., landing page, e-commerce site, web app, content site). This shapes complexity, tech stack, and team roles.
- **UNKNOWN**: Is the team co-located or distributed? (Affects communication frequency and channels.)
- **UNKNOWN**: What is the definition of done? (e.g., live on a domain, no critical bugs, mobile-responsive, WCAG AA compliant, 99.5% uptime SLA). Owner: Product owner or stakeholder.
- **UNKNOWN**: Are there external stakeholders (clients, investors, end-users)? If so, who approves the final launch, and on what timeline?
- **UNKNOWN**: What is the team's capacity? (e.g., is one person part-time? Are there other commitments?)
- **ASSUMED — Team has no external dependencies**: Other teams, services, or third-party APIs are not required for this website. If this is untrue, dependencies and handoff points must be documented.
- **ASSUMED — Code review is not blocking**: Reviews happen in parallel with other work, not serially.
- **ASSUMED — The team owns the full stack**: Backend, frontend, DevOps, and QA are not separate teams.
- **ASSUMED — Deployment is straightforward**: No complex release gates, approvals, or multi-environment rollouts beyond dev/staging/prod.

(None at this time; no claims about markets, pricing, or competitors made.)
